data.title: Herpes simplex — viva
data.summary: Viral infections · 9 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Herpes simplex** (Viral infections)_

**Q1. Types of HSV and sites?**
- HSV-1: mainly orolabial (now an increasing cause of genital herpes); HSV-2: mainly genital
- Both are alpha-herpesviruses, latent in sensory ganglia (trigeminal, sacral)

**Q2. Define primary, non-primary first episode and recurrent infection.**
- Primary: first infection in a person without antibodies to either type
- Non-primary first episode: first infection with one type in a person with antibodies to the other
- Recurrent: reactivation of latent virus

**Q3. Clinical features of primary herpetic gingivostomatitis and genital herpes?**
- Children: fever, painful oral vesicles/erosions, gingivitis, lymphadenopathy
- Genital primary: grouped painful vesicles → erosions, inguinal lymphadenopathy, fever, dysuria, urinary retention, aseptic meningitis; lasts 2–3 weeks

**Q4. What is asymptomatic shedding?**
- Virus shedding from mucosa without lesions — major source of transmission; reduced by suppressive therapy and condoms

**Q5. Complications/variants?**
- Eczema herpeticum (Kaposi varicelliform eruption — punched-out erosions on atopic skin), herpetic whitlow, herpes gladiatorum (wrestlers), keratitis, encephalitis (temporal lobe), neonatal herpes, erythema multiforme (HSV-associated), chronic ulcers in HIV, hepatitis

**Q6. Differential diagnosis of genital herpes?**
- Chancroid, primary syphilis, fixed drug eruption, Behçet ulcers, trauma, candidal balanitis, herpes zoster, erythema multiforme

**Q7. Investigations?**
- Tzanck smear: multinucleated giant cells (moulding, margination, multinucleation — 3 Ms) — cannot differentiate HSV from VZV
- PCR (most sensitive, test of choice), viral culture, DFA; type-specific serology (gG-based) for unrecognised infection

**Q8. Treatment?**
- First episode: acyclovir 400 mg three times daily × 7–10 days (or valacyclovir 1 g twice daily, famciclovir 250 mg three times daily)
- Recurrent: episodic short courses started at prodrome
- Suppressive therapy for ≥6 recurrences/year: acyclovir 400 mg twice daily or valacyclovir 500 mg–1 g daily
- Eczema herpeticum/severe: IV acyclovir 5–10 mg/kg 8-hourly; acyclovir-resistant: foscarnet/cidofovir

**Q9. Herpes in pregnancy?**
- Primary infection in third trimester carries highest neonatal risk (30–50%) — caesarean section if lesions at labour; suppressive acyclovir from 36 weeks

## Quick spotter facts
- Grouped vesicles on an erythematous base on the lip — herpes labialis

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Herpes simplex virus); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.20 and ch.131. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
